title: Deluge
summary: An ensemble episode moving from a rectal-prolapse callback and bathroom humor through friendship, paid-fan interactions, skate/music product ideas, private twins, spa sexual conduct, colonics, work, memory and burnout, then back into an unsettled orgy-production negotiation. The editorial layer preserves every explicit idea while rejecting a destructive vocabulary rewrite, accepting one decoder-loop deletion, correcting health misinformation and keeping public sexual display, filming, professional sex and each act as separate consent questions.
source_notes: The immutable audio and raw/clean transcript artifacts are present in the shared local corpus.
Three cleaner removals are empty zero-duration records.
The fourth cleaner edit correctly removes a 15-second decoder loop at 6282.96–6297.96 containing approximately 216 repeated `sword` tokens at compression ratio 40.4545.
The existing vocabulary edit `health podcast` → `self-description joke` is rejected. It invents a category absent from the source and destroys literal speech.
The indistinct closing music is marked as such rather than reconstructed into confident lyrics.
CDC says natural-membrane/lambskin condoms have pores and should not be used for HIV or STI prevention: https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/clinical-primary.htm

Mayo Clinic says nonmedical colon cleansing is unnecessary and can cause dehydration, rectal perforation, infection and dangerous electrolyte imbalance: https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/consumer-health/expert-answers/colon-cleansing/faq-20058435
Zero diarized turns and zero identity windows mean no dialogue is assigned to named speakers.
Thirty-nine narrow spans protect private twins, spouses, relatives, coworkers, fans, messages, health, schedules, venues and contact paths without removing ideas.
speaker_policy: Public participants and works may be named in editorial context where explicitly introduced, but transcript lines remain unnamed. Zero turns and zero voice windows do not support independently validated speaker attribution.
